THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a motor vehicle accident dated 23.08.2016.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 23.08.2016 petitioner along with other villagers was proceeding to coolie work in an auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-32/C-1127 ('the offending vehicle' for short).
On Chincholi-Chimmanchod main road, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-56/E-5527.
In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
In spite of prolonged treatment, petitioner is not completely cured.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Respondent No.1 has placed ex parte.
5. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement disputing that the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

7. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 & the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 11.
8.
Respondents have not led any oral or documentary evidence.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.3,08,500/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:

Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation granted under all other heads is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

13. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
14.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.

sentences.text: As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 45 years, which fact is reflected in the wound certificate.
Therefore, multiplier 14 taken by the Tribunal is correct.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal has taken her notional income at Rs.7,500/- p.m.

Since the accident is of the year 2016, based on minimum wages, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,750/-
p.m.
16.
Based on the evidence of P.W.2, the Tribunal has correctly taken the disability at 10%.
With the income at Rs.8,750/-, multiplier 14 and disability at 10%, the loss of income due to disability is at Rs.8,750/- x 12 x 14 x 10% = 1,47,000/- as against Rs.1,26,000/-.
17. Based on medical bills, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.74,300/- under the head medical expenses is correct.
At the rate of Rs.8,750/-, for a period of three months, the petitioner is entitled for compensation for a sum of Rs.26,250/- as against Rs.15,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered and the disability, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.45,000/- under the head pain and suffering and Rs.10,000/- under the head conveyance is correct.

However, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head future medical expenses, Rs.3,200/- under the head food, diet and medical attendant and Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of amenities is on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-, Rs.15,000/- and Rs.30,000/- respectively.

18. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.3,67,550/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.3,08,500/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

19. Of course as the insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the enhanced compensation with accrued interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,67,550/- as against Rs.3,08,500/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a.

(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6%
p.a. (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
(iv) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
